Binary form divides a piece into two main sections, usually repeated, with the second bringing the music home.
Theme and variations presents a tune followed by altered versions that retain something of its melody, bass or chords.
A fugue builds a piece from a theme that enters in successive voices and returns throughout the music.
A fugue subject is the main melody that the different voices introduce and repeatedly take up.
A fugal answer repeats the subject in another voice, usually a fifth higher or a fourth lower.
A countersubject is a recurring melody designed to accompany a fugue’s subject or answer.
An episode is a passage between statements of a fugue subject or returns of a refrain.
Stretto overlaps entries of a fugue subject, with the next voice starting before the previous statement has finished.
A ritornello is a returning instrumental passage, often the orchestral refrain between solo episodes in a Baroque concerto.
A passacaglia builds continuous variations over a recurring bass line or sequence of chords.
A chaconne is a set of variations built on a recurring bass or chord pattern, usually in triple time.
A scherzo is a lively piece or movement, often in triple time with a contrasting middle section called a trio.
A minuet and trio pairs two contrasting dances in triple time, then repeats the minuet.
A toccata is an instrumental showpiece, usually for keyboard, built around the player’s touch and dexterity.
A fantasia is a freely shaped piece that often sounds improvised, with sudden changes of pace and direction.
A prelude is an introductory piece, or a self-contained piece that keeps the freedom of an introduction.
